page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores and simultaneous multithreading to expose 8 vCPUs. It includes 32 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache per core. The instance provides one complimentary public IPv4 address, contains no onboard local disk storage, and operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate particularly strong per-thread compute capability alongside standard multithreaded capacity. The instance achieves top-tier scores in single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core performance metrics in Geekbench and PassMark align with median tier expectations for an 8-vCPU allocation. Memory throughput reaches 88.26 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 65.29 GB/sec for uncached writes. Small model LLM text generation shows strong execution speeds, while database operations and Redis key-value workloads run within average throughput ranges.

Because the instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, workloads rely entirely on external network-attached volumes. This architecture provides solid cost efficiency for environments needing predictable dedicated CPU execution and high single-threaded responsiveness without paying for bundled local storage arrays. VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-32 is appropriate for web application serving, backend microservices, moderate relational database hosting, continuous integration jobs, and general enterprise data processing.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.4-32 is a balanced general-purpose instance featuring 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 32 GB of system RAM, it maintains a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Architectural extensions include AVX-512 vector execution, AES cryptographic acceleration, and SHA extensions. Synthetic benchmarks highlight top-tier single-core metrics across Geekbench, stress-ng, and compression workloads, whereas multi-core throughput, Redis operations, and memory bandwidth position within median expectation bands. The instance allocates no integrated local storage or discrete GPU devices, requiring attached remote storage for disk persistence. Delivering a resource profile with dedicated execution cores, the configuration provides efficient resource utilization for enterprise web serving, microservice hosting, compilation pipelines, and transactional database tasks.
